name: lettuce head
descriptions: A full head of crisp green lettuce, just harvested from the plant.
Great for salads or tearing into leaves for immediate snacking.
effects: A cool, crunchy bite that slightly quenches thirst and fills the stomach.
Can be torn into leaves for small snacks or used as a base for meals.

name: lettuce leaf
descriptions: A single crisp leaf pulled from a lettuce head.
Light, refreshing and good as a tiny snack or garnish.
effects: A small, hydrating nibble — good for a short-lived refresh.
Useful for wrapping tiny fillings or adding crunch to a bite.

name: carrot
descriptions: A freshly harvested carrot — firm, orange, and sweet.
Crunchy and packed with natural sugars and fiber.
effects: A satisfying, crunchy snack that restores energy and fullness.
Good raw or cooked, provides a steady little boost.

name: ripe tomato
descriptions: A juicy, sun-ripened tomato still warm from the plant.
Bursting with tangy flavor and lots of juice.
effects: Juicy bite that refreshes and restores some energy.
Can be eaten raw, added to meals, or squeezed for liquid.

name: potato (tuber)
descriptions: A freshly dug potato tuber straight from the soil.
Can be used to grow other potatoes
Starchy and dense; commonly cooked but technically edible raw in small amounts.
effects: A fresh crunch, it is quite plain.
Your stomach churns as you finish eating it. That was not great.
You feel a bit sick after eating that raw.

name: strawberry
descriptions: A bright red strawberry, sweet and fragrant from the plant.
Easy to eat whole; seeds are small and embedded in the flesh.
effects: Sweet, energizing fruit that restores energy and provides a small amount of fullness.
Refreshing and good for a quick sugar boost.

name: cactus pad
descriptions: A harvested paddle-shaped green cactus pad, cleaned of spines.
Used in many cuisines; has a mild, slightly tangy flavor and viscous texture when raw.
effects: Provides hydration and fiber; slightly slimy texture but refreshing.
Often cooked, but edible raw if prepared properly.

name: prickly pear (cactus fruit)
descriptions: A sweet, juice-filled fruit that grows on certain cactus species.
Typically harvested carefully and peeled to avoid tiny glochids.
effects: Very juicy and hydrating; a sweet snack that restores both hydration and energy.
Must be handled and cleaned before eating to remove spines.

name: Edible Rose Petals
descriptions: A small pouch of freshly picked rose petals, fragrant and lightly sweet.
Suitable for tea, garnishes, or infusing into syrups and desserts.
effects: Adds a delicate floral taste when eaten or brewed into tea.
Slightly uplifting aroma can calm nerves and brighten mood.

name: Fresh Mint Sprig
descriptions: A short stem with several bright green mint leaves, fragrant and cooling.
Ideal for teas, cocktails, or to add a fresh burst of flavor to dishes.
effects: A cool, refreshing flavor that can soothe the stomach and freshen breath.
Adds a pleasant aroma and slight cooling sensation when chewed or brewed.

name: Basil Leaf Bunch
descriptions: A small bundle of tender basil leaves, aromatic and savory.
Perfect for cooking (pesto, salads, sauces) or garnishing warm dishes.
effects: Adds a rich, herbaceous flavor to food; comforting in warm dishes.
Fresh scent can be mildly invigorating and appetite-stimulating.

name: Rose Stem
descriptions: A freshly cut rose stem with a single bloom, a few glossy leaves, and a couple of small thorns along the stalk.
Commonly placed in a small vase or used as an accent in bouquets. Harvested directly from a rose plant.

name: Cut Rose Head
descriptions: A  freshly cut whole flower, scented and delicate to the touch.
Decorative, it has a deep garnet color reminicent of a sharp glass of wine.

name: Cut Sunflower Head
descriptions: A large, vibrant sunflower head with a sturdy short stem. The face is full of tightly packed seeds and bright yellow petals.
A heavy decorative piece often displayed on tabletops or hung as a rustic accent. Harvested directly from a sunflower plant.

name: onion
descriptions: A single, pungent onion, crisp and layered.
Round and papery on the outside, with a sharp, distinct aroma.
effects: The first bite is an eye-watering, throat-burning shock of pungent flavor, leaving a lingering sharpness on your tongue.
Each successive layer crunches loudly, releasing more of the acrid juice as you eat the raw, unadorned vegetable.
